title: Reserve Orchestrator dashboard — prototyping dedicated capacity controls
creator: Ethan Rodriguez
description: Design and prototype a consolidated 'Reserve Orchestrator' dashboard for Dedicated GPU capacity that surfaces health signals, autoscaling policies, burst windows, and simulated headroom planning. The goal is a single pane that lets infra and SREs quickly assess whether a reserved pool is healthy, tune autoscale rules, and run short-term burst ops without leaving the Console.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototype demonstrates list + detail view for reserved GPU pools with live health sparkline, SLO overlay, and current burst allowance.
Control surface for editing autoscaling policies (min/max, target utilization, cooldowns) with inline validation and estimated cost delta preview.
Burst booking flow that shows tokenized burst windows, affects capacity simulations, and requires confirmable audit metadata.
Simulate button runs an immediate headroom forecast for next 24h using historical telemetry and shows confidence bands and recommended actions.
Design reviewed by PM and Eng with implementation notes and a handoff-ready specs page.
Accessibility: all interactive controls reachable by keyboard and labeled for screen readers.
Performance: visuals degrade gracefully when telemetry is delayed or missing (explicit empty states and retry affordances).
research_notes: Interviewed 6 infra engineers and 3 SREs: recurring asks for quick burst reservation, preview of cost impact, and single-click rollback of autoscale changes.
Telemetry review: average pool utilization spikes align with weekday 09:00-11:00 in NA regions; KV-cache warmup period ~18-30s after scale-up observed.
Competitive review: other consoles expose autoscale knobs but not a simulation view — opportunity to differentiate with predictive headroom.
decisions: Combine pool list and detail canvas to reduce navigation friction — detail panel slides from the right instead of separate page.
Expose only safe-to-edit fields in the default view; advanced policy JSON editor behind 'Advanced' toggle.
Burst bookings require confirmation that includes estimated cost and audit note; default duration presets: 15m, 1h, 4h.
Simulations run on anonymized historical metrics and return a 95% confidence band for headroom.
next_steps: Address PM feedback on cost presentation (show per-hour and per-request deltas) — due 2025-03-04.
Create engineering spike ticket for backend simulation API: ENG-43122.
Run accessibility audit on prototype and implement ARIA labels — assigned to designer QA.
Prepare handoff doc with component tokens and interaction states for Console implementation.
Schedule demo with SRE team and gather sign-off by 2025-03-07.
risks: Backend simulation API latency could make the UX feel sluggish; fallback to cached last-run result needed.
Overloading the detail canvas with data may confuse non-operator users; need progressive disclosure.
Cost preview estimates may be mistaken for guarantees; must surface uncertainty and assumptions clearly.
accessibility_considerations: Keyboard-first interactions for burst booking and autoscale edits; ensure all charts have text alternative summaries and the simulation chart exposes data via table view.
